topic: First time at the town onsen
title_jp: {冬|ふゆ}らしい{夜|よる}の{温泉|おんせん}
context: Monday 7 December: after a cold day clearing snow in the orchard, {田中|たなか}さん takes アルちゃん to the town onsen, {鷹ノ湯|たかのゆ}, for the first time. He explains the bath rules in his few words and buys him a coffee milk afterwards.
scene: Monday, snow all day in the orchard. On the way home, {田中|たなか}さん takes you to the town onsen. You're scared of breaking a rule.

phrases.jp: もし{気分|きぶん|how one feels; mood|4}が{悪く|わるく}なったら、すぐ{言って|いって}ね。
phrases.en: If you start feeling unwell, tell me right away.
phrases.note: もし〜たら: 'if… happens'. {気分|きぶん}が{悪|わる}い = feel sick, not 'bad mood'.

phrases.jp: {湯船|ゆぶね|bathtub, the bath|3}に{入る|はいる}{前|まえ}に、{体|からだ}を{洗います|あらいます}。
phrases.en: You wash your body before getting into the bath.
phrases.note: Rule number one in every onsen and home bath.

phrases.jp: {今日|きょう}は{冬|ふゆ}らしい{寒さ|さむさ|the cold|3}ですね。
phrases.en: Today's real winter cold, isn't it?
phrases.note: Perfect small talk with neighbours in December.

phrases.jp: {入れ墨|いれずみ|tattoo|2}があったら、{入れません|はいれません}か。
phrases.en: If you have a tattoo, can't you go in?
phrases.note: Ask at reception. Many places say タトゥー; some allow a cover sticker.

phrases.jp: ああ、{生き返る|いきかえる|to come back to life|3}〜。
phrases.en: Ahh, I'm coming back to life!
phrases.note: What everyone sighs as they sink into hot water.

dialogue_setting: Monday evening, from the kei truck to the bath at {鷹ノ湯|たかのゆ}, the town onsen near the station.

dialogue.speaker: 田中さん
dialogue.jp: {今日|きょう}は{ごしたい||(Nagano dialect) = 疲れた, tired|1}{ずら||(Nagano dialect) = だろう, right?|1}。{帰り|かえり}に{温泉|おんせん|hot spring, onsen|4}{寄って|よって}くか。
dialogue.en: You must be tired today. Shall we stop at the onsen on the way home?
dialogue.note: ごしたいずら = {疲|つか}れただろう. {寄|よ}ってくか = {寄|よ}っていくか.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {行きたい|いきたい}です！でも、もしルールを{間違えたら|まちがえたら|to make a mistake|4}、どうしよう…
dialogue.en: I'd love to! But what if I get a rule wrong…

dialogue.speaker: 田中さん
dialogue.jp: {簡単|かんたん|easy, simple|4}{だに||(Nagano dialect) = だよ (emphasis)|1}。{湯船|ゆぶね|bathtub, the bath|3}に{入る|はいる}{前|まえ}に{体|からだ}を{洗う|あらう}。タオルはお{湯|ゆ}に{入れん|いれん|(casual) = 入れない, not put in|2}。
dialogue.en: It's easy. Wash yourself before you get in the bath. The towel doesn't go in the water.
dialogue.note: だに = だよ. 入れん = 入れない (casual, western Japan and Nagano).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ああ、{生き返る|いきかえる|to come back to life|3}〜。{硫黄|いおう|sulphur|2}の{匂い|におい|smell|4}がして、{温泉|おんせん}らしいですね。
dialogue.en: Ahh, I'm coming back to life! It smells of sulphur, a real onsen.

dialogue.speaker: 田中さん
dialogue.jp: {長く|ながく}{入る|はいる}と{のぼせる||to get dizzy from the heat|2}ぞ。{目|め}が{回ったら|まわったら|to turn; (目が〜) to feel dizzy|3}、{我慢|がまん|putting up with it|4}しないですぐ{出ろ|でろ}。
dialogue.en: Stay in too long and you'll get light-headed. If you feel dizzy, don't tough it out, get out at once.
dialogue.note: 出ろ: blunt command form, normal from an older man to someone close.

dialogue.speaker: 田中さん
dialogue.jp: ほれ。{風呂上がり|ふろあがり|right after a bath|3}はコーヒー{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}だに。{腰|こし|lower back, hips|3}に{手|て}を{当てて|あてて|to put (against)|3}{飲む|のむ}ずら。
dialogue.en: Here. After a bath it's coffee milk. You drink it with a hand on your hip.
dialogue.note: ほれ = ほら (here you go). だに = だよ, ずら = だろう.

listening.intro: In the changing room you see a voicemail from {恵子|けいこ}さん.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{恵子|けいこ}です。お{父さん|とうさん}と{温泉|おんせん}？いいわね。{帰り|かえり}にお{豆腐|とうふ|tofu|3}{買って|かって}きてくれる？{夕飯|ゆうはん}、{湯豆腐|ゆどうふ|simmered tofu hot pot|2}にするから。
lines.en: アルちゃん, it's {恵子|けいこ}. An onsen with Dad? Lovely. Could you buy tofu on the way back? I'm making tofu hot pot for dinner.

listening.question: {恵子|けいこ}さんは{何|なに}を{頼みましたか|たのみましたか}。
options: かえりにとうふを買ってくる
はやく家にかえってくる
おんせんでぎゅうにゅうを買う
listening.explain: She asks お{豆腐|とうふ}{買|か}ってきてくれる？ for tonight's {湯豆腐|ゆどうふ}. お{父|とう}さん is how she calls {田中|たなか}さん.

grammar.form: noun + らしい ({冬|ふゆ}らしい, {温泉|おんせん}らしい, {田中|たなか}さんらしい) · before a noun: らしい + noun ({冬|ふゆ}らしい{寒|さむ}さ) · negative: noun + らしくない ({君|きみ}らしくない)
grammar.explanation: Noun + らしい says something really is X, a perfect example of X: {冬|ふゆ}らしい{寒|さむ}さ = proper winter cold. It's not hearsay らしい ('apparently'). And っぽい means 'looks like X' (maybe it isn't); らしい means 'is X, and very X'.

examples.jp: そんなこと{言う|いう}なんて、{君|きみ}らしくないよ。
examples.en: Saying something like that isn't like you.

examples.jp: {今日|きょう}は{春|はる}らしい{暖かい|あたたかい}{日|ひ}だね。
examples.en: Today's a real spring day, nice and warm.

quiz.question: 12{月|がつ}になって、やっと{冬|ふゆ}＿＿{寒さ|さむさ|the cold|3}になった。
quiz.en: Now it's December, it's finally properly winter-cold.
quiz.explain: Noun + らしい + noun: {冬|ふゆ}らしい{寒|さむ}さ, no の in between.

quiz_more.question: {田中|たなか}さんは{何|なに}も{言わないで|いわないで}{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}を{買って|かって}くれた。{田中|たなか}さん＿＿ね。
quiz_more.en: {田中|たなか}さん bought me milk without a word. So typical of him.
quiz_more.explain: He is {田中|たなか}さん, acting exactly like himself → らしい. っぽい/みたい would mean someone who only resembles him.

quiz_more.question: そんなに{怒る|おこる}なんて、{健太|けんた}＿＿ね。
quiz_more.en: Getting that angry isn't like {健太|けんた}.
quiz_more.explain: らしい conjugates like an い-adjective: negative らしくない.

kanji.where: The sign over the door between the reception and the baths at {鷹ノ湯|たかのゆ}.
kanji.breakdown: {脱衣所|だついじょ}: 脱 take off + 衣 clothes + 所 place → 'the place where you take off your clothes'.
kanji.related: {男湯|おとこゆ} = men's bath, {女湯|おんなゆ} = women's bath (on the blue and red curtains).

tip.title: The after-bath milk
tip.body: Old onsen and {銭湯|せんとう} always have a fridge of glass-bottle coffee milk. Drinking it in one go, hand on hip, is a joke every Japanese person knows. Do it once: the locals will love you.

challenge.prompt: Back home, {恵子|けいこ}さん: 「{鷹ノ湯|たかのゆ}、どうだった？」 Tell her it smelled of sulphur, a real onsen.

options.jp: {硫黄|いおう}の{匂|にお}いがして、{温泉|おんせん}らしい{温泉|おんせん}でした！
options.why: Noun + らしい + noun: a true, typical onsen. Polite past to {恵子|けいこ}さん.

options.jp: {硫黄|いおう}の{匂|にお}いがして、{温泉|おんせん}のらしい{温泉|おんせん}でした！
options.why: No の: the noun goes straight before らしい.

options.jp: {硫黄|いおう}の{匂|にお}いがして、{温泉|おんせん}らしかったそうです！
options.why: そうです is hearsay: you were there yourself.

options.jp: {硫黄|いおう}の{匂|にお}いがして、{温泉|おんせん}っぽい{温泉|おんせん}でした！
options.why: っぽい sounds like it only resembled an onsen.

challenge.model_answer: {硫黄|いおう|sulphur|2}の{匂い|におい|smell|4}がして、{温泉|おんせん}らしい{温泉|おんせん}でした！
challenge.explanation: 〜の{匂|にお}いがする is how Japanese says 'it smells of…'. {温泉|おんせん}らしい{温泉|おんせん} praises it as a real, classic onsen, which is exactly the compliment you want. でした keeps it polite for {恵子|けいこ}さん.

vocab.note: {温|おん} warm + {泉|せん} spring. {温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}る = take an onsen bath.

vocab.en: to make a mistake, get wrong
vocab.note: Transitive: {道|みち}を{間違|まちが}える. {間違|まちが}い = a mistake.
{湯|ゆ} hot water + {船|ふね} boat. {湯船|ゆぶね}につかる = soak in the bath.

vocab.en: to come back to life; feel refreshed
vocab.note: {生|い}きる live + {返|かえ}る return. Said after a hot bath or a cold beer.
〜の{匂|にお}いがする = it smells of… Bad smells are often written {臭|にお}い.
{目|め}が{回|まわ}る = to feel dizzy; also 'so busy my head spins'.
{我慢|がまん}する. {我慢|がまん}しないで = don't force yourself to bear it.
{気分|きぶん}が{悪|わる}い = feel sick. {気分|きぶん}がいい = feel good.
{風呂|ふろ} bath + {上|あ}がる get out. {風呂上|ふろあ}がりのビール is a classic.

kanji_study.parts: 氵 water radical + 昜 the sun rising high over the horizon → water warmed by the sun: hot water.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 場 (place, as in {駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}): 場 has 土 earth on the left, 湯 has 氵 water.

kanji_study.parts: A small 口 inside a big 口 → a whirlpool going round and round: turn. Also counts times ('rounds').
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 固 (hard): 固 has 古 inside the box, 回 has a small 口.

extras.title: Onsen words
extras.intro: What you'll read on the signs.

items.note: Best in snow: hot water, cold head.

items.jp: かけ{湯|ゆ|pouring water over yourself|2}
items.note: Scoop water over your body before getting in.

items.jp: {貸切風呂|かしきりぶろ|private bath (rented)|2}
items.note: Good for couples, families, or tattoos.

extras.title: Bath and body
extras.title_jp: お{風呂|ふろ}と{体|からだ}
extras.intro: Little words for how a bath makes you feel.

items.jp: {湯冷め|ゆざめ|getting chilled after a bath|2}する
items.en: to get chilled after a bath
items.note: Why {恵子|けいこ}さん says dry your hair in winter.

items.jp: {肩|かた|shoulders|4}まで{浸かる|つかる|to soak|3}
items.en: to soak up to your shoulders
items.note: What parents tell kids in the bath.
Warm all over after the onsen.
